BL3 is the culmination of Gearbox's tradition of gameplay iteration. Each, successive sequel does something to improve on the previous game and BL3 is no exception. At the time BL3 released, it had the best gunplay and movement in the franchise. Even after the release of BL4 which arguably has better movement and comparable gunplay, I frequently return to 3. I believe it is the absolute representation of a Borderlands title, from the gameplay and multifaceted, legendary loot to the disparate environments and zany, memorable characters. BL4 was lacking in the latter two departments. 3 has a few narrative choices that I did not wholly agree with but in totality, it's the best Borderlands game. And yes, I place it above BL2, which has the stronger base game narrative. BL3 simply holds up better with its more modern movement and shooting features. It also has the best collection of DLC story packs, which outshine the narrative of the base game.

PS Ignore my low gameplay time. I have about 400 hours or so on Xbox. I just recently purchased the game on Steam so I could play on my handheld.

Gameplay is great, story feels like it was written by 15 year olds. The story itself feels like juvenile humor and it’s really hard to give a shit about. If you’re mainly interested in the game play it’s worth a try but the story will probably not engage you.

I honestly wish there was a neutral stance on "Do you recommend this game?" instead of a Yes or No.

citations.review_text:
Borderlands 3 is still an absolute blast, even in 2026! The graphics hold up incredibly well, the art style is timeless, and the game still looks fantastic.

The gunplay is satisfying, the world is packed with things to explore, and there's an insane amount of loot to collect. The humor, characters and chaotic gameplay make it just as entertaining today as it was at launch.

If you enjoy looter shooters with tons of content, crazy weapons and endless fun, Borderlands 3 is definitely worth playing.

Greetings, flesh-sacks! It is I, CLAPTRAP, your beloved general, master of ceremonies, and definitely-not-annoying guide to the galaxy!
Since my programming forbids me from doing anything useful like climbing stairs, I have instead written the ultimate, completely unbiased review of Borderlands 3. Step aside, human critics! A real cybernetic masterpiece is about to break it down for you.

THE GAMEPLAY: 10/10 (Just like my dance moves!)

First things first: the shooting and looting are absolutely fantastic. The master-class weapon variety lets you fire everything from pistols that scream insults to guns that spawn more guns when you reload. They finally added mantling and slide mechanics, meaning you can parkour around the battlefield with the grace of a gazelle—or at least the grace of me if I had actual legs instead of a single, squeaky unicycle wheel!
The action skills are bigger and louder than ever. You can stomp around in a giant mech, summon elemental sirens, or sic cyber-beasts on bandits. It feels so good it almost makes me forget about that time I was brutally reprogrammed to be a cruise ship door closer!

THE STORY: 6/10 (Needs 500% more Claptrap)

Now, let's talk about the plot. We leave Pandora and head into the stars aboard Sanctuary III, which is a glorious spaceship mainly because I am on it. However, our main villains are the Calypso Twins—a pair of hyper-cringey siren streamers who literally murder people for "likes." Honestly, I haven't seen a more annoying, desperate cry for attention since... well, since my last birthday party when nobody showed up because I "forgot" to send invitations and also everyone hates me.
The dialogue can drag on a bit, forcing you to stand around listening to NPCs talk when you could be out there blowing things up. Plus, they gave me a new voice actor, which some organic beings complained about—but personally, I think my vocal modulators have never sounded more pristine and majestic!

THE VERDICT

Borderlands 3 is an ab…

The player can't hate the characters they're supposed to be fighting for. I cannot recall another game where I've felt the same insane urge to join the "evil faction" and mercilessly annihilate all my previous "allies". Slaughtering Lilith, Ava, Tannis and all the other annoying, narcissistic girlbosses in this dogshit game would bring me a greater wave of pleasure than killing any of its villains ever did.

You can make a fun game, but a fun game where you're constantly bombarded with humiliation rituals, unfunny jokes and annoying characters that treat you like a side hoe gets stale very fast, no matter how shiny the loot is or how well made the movement is. You can try to ignore it, as I've been told to do, but it isn't enough. I just can't bring myself to turn my brain completely off. There's always that annoying, mosquito-like buzz in your ear. It feels like Randy is forcing you on the cuck chair next to his, watching as a black man delivers pleasure to his wife for the first time in her life.

Too many women and browns. Needs more whites who aren't punching bags.
Gunplay seems best in the series so far, story eh.

citations.review_text: People overexaggerate the story being that bad when you can just go into settings and turn "dialogue" to 0, you're welcome.

Surprisingly, I had a lot of fun with the game. I wasn't a huge fan of BL1 and BL2 - both were kinda mid in my mind.
I remember there being a huge hate bandwagon about the 2 main villains on release - and yeah, the dialogue and writing in this game is mostly bad, cringy and unfunny, with a decent amount of gross out "humor" to boot.
But the gameplay and gunplay really do carry this game, with visuals (despite the ugly cel shading) and audio also being pretty good, and they all are better here than the previous two games by a wide margin.

[h3]The guns, loot and gameplay[/h3]
Undeniably the best part. Yeah, it starts slow with guns that have poor accuracy, like in previous games, but it picks up fast and by the second half I was drowning in legendries, so much so that I was wiping most bosses, including the final story boss, in under a minute, just because I happened to kill an optional animal mini-boss on the way there.

I did like the new feature of guns having alternative firing modes. Most of the time its something boring - a burst/auto switch, but for some guns they have cool gimmicks like the underbarrel grenade launcher or a shotgun, elemental type switch, auto aim puck, etc., depending on the gun manufacturer.

The guns are kinda weird though.
Most pistols seem to just be SMGs. This makes the SMG archetype pointless. Rocket Launchers also appear to be extremely underwhelming, at least in my playthrough and build, they did no more damage that regular guns, and had extremely poor ammo economy and slow firing speed, making them useless in my view.
Then there are the weapon manufacturers. At least half of them have weird gimmicks - slow charge up times, throw-away reloads, overheat mechanics, slow projectiles, etc.

What this all culminates in is that I stuck with like 3 "boring" manufactures, and mostly pistols and assault rifles, because that's what was most effective. The other 6 manufacturers and 4 gun archetypes were just immediately trashed, because they ar…

claims.claim: The main campaign story and writing are described as poor, weak, or annoying.

citations.review_text:
[The DLC is very good, worth playing if you make it though the story!!!] 
 Long time Borderlands player, this game is really good; despite the really annoying, repetitive story. The gameplay of this particular title is one of, if not the most customizable and fun takes on the running, gunning and looting that this franchise known for. I've played this on PC an PS4, for a combined 500 hrs- and I can say, the lengthy, forced interactions with the cast will get annoying and you will start to just ignore the bad dialogue and writing like the rest of us. Treasure every moment the game just lets you shoot stuff with the cool character you're playing as. 
Main story: A generous 4/10 
Gameplay: 8/10 Gun go burr

-CONS-
> story isn't as good as other borderlands games - notably borderlands 2 (no villain will ever truly be as good as handsome jack)
> sometimes terribly cringey dialogue

-PROS-
> everything else

seriously! this game has its bad points, but overall they don't affect the game at all! there is some terrible writing, but there is also some GREAT writing (some points I literally laughed out loud) 
on every other point of this game other than story and dialogue, this is hands down the best borderlands in the series for gameplay, DLC, character builds, crazy guns and modifiers, bosses and endgame

GET THIS GAME (on sale if possible)

The sad paradox of BL3 is that it features the best gameplay in the series, balanced out by the worst story to boot.

Gearbox were a couple of steps away from making a generational masterpiece but somehow managed to cook up the most underwhelming narrative, annoyingly bland characters, and AI-level dialogue that silenced most of the redeeming qualities that the game had going for itself.

The strangest part is that the DLC content in this game is absolutely phenomenal, and for the most part, feels like a polished product when looking back at the base game campaign.

The story is what it is, but in the defense of Gearbox (yes, I cannot believe I'm typing that), there is a great game under the surface of the awful storytelling choices they made. 

On the other hand, the gameplay is addictive like crack cocaine, which is unironically the best in the series with its tech tree builds and unique weapon variety. BL2 andies will take offence to this, but hey, you can't win them all, so f_ck them as far as I'm concerned. Their judgement holds the same value as legendary drops in this game. 

I remember playing through the entire game and DLC content with one of my friends, and we had an absolute blast, which the Discord mod-level dialogue couldn't touch. 

Come to your own conclusions after trying it out.

9/15/26 Update: After starting a new save and playing through some of the DLC's, it utterly bamboozles me how they could have failed so hard on the main game story but won so hard with the DLC's. Every single one (Yes, even the 3rd, imo, despite most of the community not liking it) has good story and quick pacing considering its a DLC. 


By far the best in the franchise. I huffed the "BL4 IS GOOD" Copium for about 80 hours until realizing BL3 is just superior. Not gonna rant about BL4, thats its own review but yes, the story for BL3 is dogcrap. Install a dialogue/cutscene skipper and the game is immediately a 9/10 instead of a 5/10. The gameplay and DLC's make up for the lackluster main story. (Except Season Pass 2, its kinda bad. just buy the first one). Base game is also great, but mods like REBORN or REBALANDS make the imperfect balance better (or worse, I prefer rebalands balance imo) and some skills actually usable. IF your wondering whether to play BL4 or BL3, go BL3 every day of the week. BL4 is worth maybe one playthrough and thats it.

[The DLC is very good, worth playing if you make it though the story!!!] 
 Long time Borderlands player, this game is really good; despite the really annoying, repetitive story. The gameplay of this particular title is one of, if not the most customizable and fun takes on the running, gunning and looting that this franchise known for. I've played this on PC an PS4, for a combined 500 hrs- and I can say, the lengthy, forced interactions with the cast will get annoying and you will start to just ignore the bad dialogue and writing like the rest of us. Treasure every moment the game just lets you shoot stuff with the cool character you're playing as. 
Main story: A generous 4/10 
Gameplay: 8/10 Gun go burr

Borderlands 3, truth be told I really enjoy this game. The looting, shooting, traversal, level design, enemy design, sound design and soundtrack. Pretty much everything to do with the core gameplay is fantastic. The drop rates and selection for items I personally think is the best of all the BL games, it tows that line of,  you will get legendaries to drop a lot but whether you get good parts rolls determines the viability of them which I greatly enjoy and tickles the loot goblin in me. The Gunplay is still the slight edge of wackyness and realism that previous titles brought, and each vault hunter is viable and has very fun unique action skills. Swapping between those action skills and crafting builds I think is the strongest here over the previous games.

Now the story, is all over the place for me. The main campaign storyline is definitely the weakest its ever been, but there are still many many likable characters (along with a few unlikeable) that are still written decent for what they're trying to be. The DLCs are where they definitely improved greatly on the story telling, and actually impressed me with how much better the writting for the DLCs is. 

In short, Its a very fun game to play, don't get too attached to the story/characters, blast psyco's in the dome and get Shlootin!

The shooting is genuinely great, best in the series, no argument there. Problem is everything around it. The villains are twitch streamers, every NPC talks in memes that were already dead in 2019, and I started skipping cutscenes about ten hours in. I stayed for the loot, not for the game.

The sad paradox of BL3 is that it features the best gameplay in the series, balanced out by the worst story to boot.

Gearbox were a couple of steps away from making a generational masterpiece but somehow managed to cook up the most underwhelming narrative, annoyingly bland characters, and AI-level dialogue that silenced most of the redeeming qualities that the game had going for itself.

The strangest part is that the DLC content in this game is absolutely phenomenal, and for the most part, feels like a polished product when looking back at the base game campaign.

The story is what it is, but in the defense of Gearbox (yes, I cannot believe I'm typing that), there is a great game under the surface of the awful storytelling choices they made. 

On the other hand, the gameplay is addictive like crack cocaine, which is unironically the best in the series with its tech tree builds and unique weapon variety. BL2 andies will take offence to this, but hey, you can't win them all, so f_ck them as far as I'm concerned. Their judgement holds the same value as legendary drops in this game. 

I remember playing through the entire game and DLC content with one of my friends, and we had an absolute blast, which the Discord mod-level dialogue couldn't touch. 

Come to your own conclusions after trying it out.

Not gonna rant about BL4, thats its own review but yes, the story for BL3 is dogcrap. Install a dialogue/cutscene skipper and the game is immediately a 9/10 instead of a 5/10. The gameplay and DLC's make up for the lackluster main story. (Except Season Pass 2, its kinda bad. just buy the first one). Base game is also great, but mods like REBORN or REBALANDS make the imperfect balance better (or worse, I prefer rebalands balance imo) and some skills actually usable. IF your wondering whether to play BL4 or BL3, go BL3 every day of the week. BL4 is worth maybe one playthrough and thats it.

claims.claim: Mission dialogue and interactions are described as lengthy, forced, or requiring players to wait through unskippable talking sequences.

citations.review_text:
[The DLC is very good, worth playing if you make it though the story!!!] 
 Long time Borderlands player, this game is really good; despite the really annoying, repetitive story. The gameplay of this particular title is one of, if not the most customizable and fun takes on the running, gunning and looting that this franchise known for. I've played this on PC an PS4, for a combined 500 hrs- and I can say, the lengthy, forced interactions with the cast will get annoying and you will start to just ignore the bad dialogue and writing like the rest of us. Treasure every moment the game just lets you shoot stuff with the cool character you're playing as. 
Main story: A generous 4/10 
Gameplay: 8/10 Gun go burr

Good entry in the franchise for new and returning borderlands looter-shooter enjoyers, the mechanics are more of what we love with that modern AAA game polish. The way they implemented action skill variety between the different heroes and the extra 4 skill trees in leu of added dlc characters is fresh and I think a great change. There is one fatal flaw, that being the story. My god, I get that borderlands always had a bit of that quirky millenial-type humour but this is just miserable too listen to. What definetly doesn't help is the fact that the mission-dialogue is always agonisignly long, with the added bonus of you needing to interact-listen-interact-listen  before you can even start running to the next sequence of interacting and listening. I HIGHLY reccomend playing with the voices disabled and playing a yt video in the background while playing this game, personally I found it 10x more enjoyable that way. 7/10

I will recommend this title, if you can play with at least one friend (especially if you have fun together). We can see many upgrades in this game like better shooting feeling, graphic increase, more freedom moving around (etc. climbing). Very good thing in this game is Mayhem mode, which increase difficulty level of your adventure and scale enemies to your level (so you can enjoy running through dlcs or later missions); leveling is faster and easier than previous parts, and you don't need to re-run whole game again, if you use ''mayhem mode'' you don't need to worry to get 72lvl. First off we start on normal mode and we can set lobby for two options (separate loot for all members or no separate). After finishing game once, you can set in game settings ''True Vault Hunter Mode'', but i didn't use it once, so you need to check for yourself or on web. Last very good and very helpful thing we can set in options is auto-sell ''common->purple rarity items, so no longer need to run to vendors many times) and you can find a lot of gold stuff just killing enemies.
Game is boring and long. I think after pre-sequel they started to like long voice talks and slowing progress. Game have many posivite aspects, but i didn't enjoy it enough to recommend for solo playing (even i maxed out achievements, but for my own purpose).
If you ever played Killing Floor, for me Borderlands 3 in compare to Borderlands 2 is like Killing Floor 2 for KF1 (many upgrades, but worse, more colorful and annoiying robots). Shooting, looting and exploring was fine, but story and overall feelings was mixed, and i was exhausted playing it.
